column1: # The technical terms of the English commentary: the English of this translation, the Arabic and its transliteration,
# Robbins's English for Ptolemy's term (with the Greek where Robbins prints it), and what the term means.

column5: meaning
The five planets, Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus and Mercury; with the sun and the moon, the seven.
The sun and the moon.
Jupiter and Venus; Ptolemy counts the moon with them.
Saturn and Mars.
The ascendant, the middle of the sky, the setting point and the cardine of the earth.
The degree of the ecliptic rising on the eastern horizon.
The degree of the ecliptic culminating on the meridian.
The degree of the ecliptic setting on the western horizon.
The degree opposite the middle of the sky, below the earth.
In one of the places that follow the cardines in the daily motion: the third, sixth, ninth and twelfth.

The relations of two places by conjunction, sextile, quadrature, trine or opposition, at 0°, 60°, 90°, 120° and 180°; «on the diameter» is opposition. To «share in a configuration» is to stand in one of them.
A planet applies to a planet that it is approaching and separates from one that it has passed.
The ways in which one planet prevails over another (chapter 11).
The diurnal or the nocturnal party of the planets: the sun, Jupiter and Saturn by day; the moon, Venus and Mars by night; Mercury in both.
The places where a planet has authority: its houses, exaltation, triplicity, terms and faces.
A planet's claims to govern a place: triplicity, house, exaltation, term, and phase or configuration.
The planet with the most shares in a place, which governs the matter that the place signifies.
The sign of which a planet is lord; also one of the twelve places counted from the ascendant, such as the house of the brothers.
The sign, and the degree in it, where a planet's power is raised.
One of the four sets of three signs in trine, with its lords by day and by night (the table of f. 80v).
The unequal parts of each sign assigned to the five planets (the table of f. 80v).
The thirds of a sign, ten degrees each, assigned to planets (the table of f. 80v).

column1: the lot of good fortune, the lot of fortune
column5: The point that stands from the ascendant as the moon stands from the sun (chapter 24).
The place or planet from which the length of life is directed (chapter 24); a Persian word.
«The lord of the house» in Persian: in the doctrine of others than Ptolemy, the planet that gives the years of life (chapter 24).
Carrying the haylāj or another place through the signs by the ascensions, a year for each degree (chapters 24 and 37).
The places whose meeting with the directed haylāj ends life (chapters 24 and 36).
The planet or ray that a directed place meets, and the ray that a planet casts from one of the configurations.

column1: attributed to the mornings, to the evenings
column4: matutine, vespertine; morning star, evening star
column5: Rising before the sun, or setting after it.
Relative to the horizon, rising or setting; relative to the sun, before or after it.
Too near the sun to be seen.
Planets that accompany a luminary (chapter 30).
The ascending and the descending node of the moon.

column4: the House of the Good Daemon (δαίμων)
column5: The eleventh place.

column4: the House of the Evil Daemon
column5: The twelfth place.
The ninth place.

column1: the tropical, fixed and bicorporeal signs
column5: Aries, Cancer, Libra and Capricorn; Taurus, Leo, Scorpio and Aquarius; Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius and Pisces.
The degrees of the equator that rise with a stretch of the ecliptic, in the clime of the birth or in the right sphere.
The sphere as seen from the equator, where the ascensions are right ascensions.
The time when the sun returns to its place at the birth (chapter 53 of the *Zīj*); its months and days are those of the table of f. 80r.
A planet's entry into one of the places of the times (chapter 37).
The planets that govern a period of life (chapter 37).
The person whose nativity is considered; also «the child».
